title: Microservices Architecture Rules
description: Rules governing the microservices phase. Autonomous deployability is the core principle. Service mesh readiness is mandatory.

rules.title: True Independent Deployability
rules.description: Each service MUST deploy independently with no coordination required with any other service. Contract-first approach ensures backward compatibility.
rules.rationale: Microservices exists only when services can truly evolve independently. Coordinated deployments indicate premature Microservices adoption.
rules.validationQuery: Each service has independent CI/CD. No service has a deployment dependency on another service's release schedule.

rules.title: Service Mesh Readiness
rules.description: All services MUST be deployed behind a service mesh (Istio, Linkerd, or equivalent) or equivalent sidecar infrastructure. mTLS MUST be enforced for all in-cluster communication.
rules.rationale: Service mesh provides observability, traffic management, and security at the infrastructure level. core/ADR-0013 covers cloud topology and DR.
rules.validationQuery: Service-to-service communication uses mTLS. Service mesh provides routing, retries, and circuit breaking.

rules.title: Bulkhead Pattern per Service
rules.description: Each service MUST implement bulkhead isolation: resource pools (connections, threads) are isolated per upstream dependency.
rules.rationale: Bulkheads prevent a single upstream failure from consuming all resources and causing cascading failures.
rules.validationQuery: Each service has dedicated connection pools per upstream dependency. One upstream timeout does not exhaust shared pool.

rules.title: Fallback Behavior for All External Calls
rules.description: All inter-service calls MUST have defined fallback behavior when the downstream service is unavailable. Graceful degradation is required.
rules.rationale: Microservices services must remain functional even when other services are degraded. No hard failure propagation to end user.
rules.validationQuery: All downstream calls have fallback: cached response, default value, or degraded mode. E2E tests validate fallback paths.

rules.title: Contract Tests for All Inter-Service Contracts
rules.description: All inter-service contracts (synchronous gRPC/REST and asynchronous events) MUST have contract tests (Pact or equivalent) that validate backward compatibility before merge.
rules.rationale: Contract tests prevent breaking changes from reaching production. Consumer-driven contract testing is the gold standard.
rules.validationQuery: Contract tests exist for all inter-service contracts. CI fails on breaking contract changes.

rules.title: Service Owns Its Data — No Shared Persistence
rules.description: Each service owns its data store exclusively. No shared databases, no cross-service table access, no data leakage through APIs.
rules.rationale: Data sovereignty is the foundation of service independence. Shared persistence creates hidden coupling that defeats F3.
rules.validationQuery: Each service has isolated persistence. No cross-service database queries. Data access only through published API.

rules.title: Service-Level Observability with SLOs
rules.description: Each service MUST define and monitor its SLOs (Service Level Objectives). Error budget tracking is required. Dashboard per service is mandatory.
rules.rationale: SLOs provide objective health metrics per service. Without them, there's no data-driven basis for reliability decisions.
rules.validationQuery: SLO dashboard per service. Error budget tracking active. Alerts fire when SLO is at risk.

rules.title: Service-Level On-Call Ownership
rules.description: Each service MUST have a designated on-call owner. Runbooks exist for all common failure scenarios. Incident response time <= 15 minutes.
rules.rationale: Microservices requires service-level ownership. Shared on-call across all services loses the independence benefit.
rules.validationQuery: On-call roster per service exists. Runbooks documented and tested.

exitGate.description: Microservices does not exit. Microservices is the terminal architecture phase. Any further evolution requires new architectural decision via ADR.
